parts.transcript: S2: guide Hazel gives do's and don'ts for Muna Island. Taxi tips: no set rate, up to you = as much as you feel right (11=A). Medical service is not complimentary - you pay/it will be charged (12=A; buy insurance before you leave). Tap water is safe but has a weird/unusual taste as it contains minerals (13=C). Bottled water: make sure the sealed lid is untouched - the bottle is not always sealed (14=B; locals refill). Bus: roads bumpy, causes nausea - not comfortable (15=C; they are on time). Can't see destination on the bus or at the stop - ask/check with the driver (16=B). Before renting a car, compare prices online in advance (17=C; hotel booking overcharges). Important to check what the price covers/includes (18=B; mileage unlimited, fuel excluded). Find a taxi by stopping/waving one on the street (19=C; reserving means a wait). No meter - negotiate/agree the price with the driver in advance (20=C).

parts.transcript: S3 (== Mock 37 S3): Jeannie and Dan discuss her research on music's effect on consumer behaviour in restaurants. Topic: effect of music on consumers/behaviour (21=A). In all five restaurants the music volume is unchanged/uniform (22=B). The first questionnaire questions act as distractors - to disguise the purpose of the survey (23=C). She based the questionnaire on a previous student's assignment found by a dictionary = a previous study (24=A). Main reasons for choosing a restaurant: seat capacity (E, not crowded) + comparing rivals online = competitors nearby (A) (25/26=A,E; service only 12%, location no longer matters). Attitudes to music: no music -> think it's not worth the price/charges too much (27=D); jazz -> stay longer, order more = spend more money (28=A); classical -> finish quickly and leave right after eating (29=E); pop -> come back again (30=C).

parts.title: Life on the International Space Station
parts.transcript: S4: presentation on early life aboard the International Space Station. Early impressions (better than expected): air smelt fresh (31, not stale); temperature easy to adjust; food praised for its variety (32); communication (33) with Earth was clear/reliable = efficient. Problems: noisy air filters interrupted sleep = lack of sleep (34); Velcro failed so objects floated; incompatible systems - couldn't mix the water (35) from different systems due to preservatives; the tools (36) provided weren't always suitable; instructions (37) for maintenance were hard to access/read (on the back of equipment). Improvements: equipment needs more extensive testing (38); language training needs practice understanding the controller's accent (39); designers should put less emphasis on safety (40) and more on operating issues.
